claims.claim: Lorne Doerkson said his first big bill will raise the basic personal exemption to $32,000 so British Columbians pay no tax on earnings up to that amount, and the Sun reported the change must be made by January 1 to apply in the 2027 tax year.
claims.episode_span: his first big bill will raise the basic personal exemption to $32,000
claims.source_title: B.C. premier-designate Lorne Doerkson hints at a fall legislative session
claims.supporting_quote: In terms of legislation, Doerkson said his first big bill will raise the basic personal exemption to $32,000, meaning British Columbians will not pay any tax on their earnings up to that amount.

claims.claim: Doerkson said that on day one the government will launch an independent review of provincial finances, that the deficit is nearly $14 billion, and that B.C. has had eight credit downgrades in three years.
claims.episode_span: citing a deficit of nearly $14 billion and eight credit downgrades in three years
claims.source_title: B.C. premier-designate Lorne Doerkson hints at a fall legislative session
claims.supporting_quote: On day one, we will launch an independent review of the province’s finances. The deficit, as you know, is nearly $14 billion, and B.C. has had eight credit downgrades in three years.

claims.claim: Daily Hive reported NDP deficit forecasts of $13.8 billion, $12.7 billion and $12 billion over three fiscal years, debt of $180.9 billion this fiscal year and almost $236 billion before the end of the decade, and about $89 billion when Eby became premier in late 2022.
claims.episode_span: total provincial debt expected at $180.9 billion by the end of this fiscal year
claims.source_title: I will govern for everyone: B.C. premier-elect Lorne Doerkson lays out priorities
claims.supporting_quote: Doerkson pointed to the BC NDP’s forecast of a historic $13.8-billion annual budget deficit for the 2026/2027 fiscal year, followed by $12.7 billion in 2027/2028 and $12 billion in 2028/2029.

claims.claim: More than 1,200 workers walked off the job at Highland Valley Copper near Logan Lake after contract talks failed, and Teck says operations continue at reduced capacity.
claims.episode_span: More than 1,200 workers have walked off the job at Highland Valley Copper near Logan Lake
claims.source_title: More than 1,200 workers walk off job at B.C. copper mine after contract talks fail
claims.supporting_quote: More than 1,200 workers have walked off the job at Highland Valley Copper near Logan Lake, B.C., after contract talks broke down. Teck says operations are continuing at reduced capacity.

claims.claim: About 150 Sutherland Secondary students were stranded for hours Friday night after their party boat ran aground in Burrard Inlet.
claims.episode_span: About 150 Sutherland Secondary School students celebrating their graduating year were stranded for hours
claims.source_title: North Vancouver graduates-to-be have a night to remember as party boat gets stuck in the mud
claims.supporting_quote: About 150 Sutherland Secondary School students who were celebrating their graduating year were stranded for hours on Friday night after their party boat ran aground in the Burrard Inlet.

claims.claim: A record 15 Punjab-origin candidates were elected in British Columbia, 11 Conservative and four NDP, passing the 2024 high of 14.
claims.episode_span: a record 15 Indian-origin candidates from Punjab were elected to the B.C. legislature
claims.source_title: Conservatives sweep Surrey as record 15 Punjab-origin candidates win in British Columbia
claims.supporting_quote: A record 15 Indian-origin candidates hailing from Punjab have been elected to the British Columbia legislature as the Conservative Party won the provincial election and defeated the New Democratic Party (NDP) on October 24. Of these, 11 are Conservatives and four are from the NDP.

claims.claim: Adrian Dix, re-elected in Vancouver-Kingsway, said it was obviously a mistake to call the election.
claims.episode_span: Obviously it was a mistake to call the election
claims.source_title: BC NDP party faithful dismayed at impacts of Eby’s snap election
claims.supporting_quote: Other MLAs felt the sudden election (two years ahead of the scheduled date) was unwarranted and caused difficulty, including long-time NDP MLA Adrian Dix (who on October 24 was re-elected in Vancouver-Kingsway for the seventh time), who bluntly told TV media that “obviously it was a mistake to call the election”.

claims.claim: The Minnesota Wild beat the Vancouver Canucks 4-2, Hughes recorded his 500th point, and the Canucks lost their tenth straight game.
claims.episode_span: The Minnesota Wild beat the Vancouver Canucks 4-2 on Sunday at Rogers Arena
claims.source_title: Hughes scores in return to Vancouver as Canucks lose to Wild
claims.supporting_quote: Quinn Hughes notched the 500th point of his NHL career in his return to Vancouver, and his Minnesota Wild doubled up the Canucks 4-2 on Sunday.

claims.claim: Mia Pante scored twice in Vancouver Rise FC's 3-2 win over Calgary Wild FC on Sunday in Burnaby.
claims.episode_span: Mia Pante scored twice as Vancouver Rise FC beat Calgary Wild FC 3-2
claims.source_title: Mia Pante scores brace as Rise defeat Wild, move into final NSL playoff spot
claims.supporting_quote: Mia Pante scored twice to lead Vancouver Rise FC to a 3-2 win over Calgary Wild FC on Sunday in Northern Super League action in Burnaby, B.C.

claims.claim: Environment Canada forecast a high of 12 for Vancouver on Monday with no watches or warnings, and current conditions of cloudy and 9.7 degrees.
claims.episode_span: No weather watches or warnings are in effect; it is cloudy and 9.7 degrees now, with a high of 12 today
claims.supporting_quote: No watches or warnings in effect. Current conditions: Cloudy, 9.7°C.
